judgments.exegetical_claim: The Gospel can become fruitful through weak disciples who remain among those to whom they are sent; the Thessalonians show received faith becoming exemplary conduct during affliction. Continuing dependence on grace does not postpone faithful action.
judgments.text_substitution_test: The movement depends on the woman hiding leaven in much meal after failed seed and hostile weeds, then the Epistle moving from imitation to example in actual affliction and ending with the risen Son awaited. Replacing these readings with unrelated ones would remove the actual mechanism and evidence. The Collect specifies words and deeds; the Secret supplies cleansing, renewal, direction and protection; the two cries from the depths and Postcommunion retain ongoing dependence. These are substantive uses, not decorative verse mentions.
judgments.source_fidelity: Chrysostom explicitly connects leaven with mixture/contact and challenges the miracle excuse by apostolic freedom from wealth/glory. His Thessalonian exposition distinguishes grievous events from Spirit-given joy; the homily does not demand an untroubled appearance. Aquinas expressly connects faith with work and labor and hope with endurance, and identifies resurrection and freedom from future punishment in 1:10. The homily does not attribute its complete Mass connection or patient-speech application to either author.
judgments.oral_clarity: Continuous finished speech, clear scene and recoverable transitions, no inline citations, unexplained Latin, dates recited aloud, invented anecdotes, clerical identity, stage directions, or dependence on visible notes. Named authorities contribute developed reasoning while the preacher carries the argument.
judgments.pastoral_fruit_and_hope: One practicable second-person response—patient truthful speech when hostility tempts contempt—grows from the Collect and exemplary conduct, and recognizes that the hearer cannot control another person’s reception. Ending reaches resurrection and the risen Son rather than stopping at present influence.
